caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 78 of 2001
lawyer:
Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record - For the Petitioners 
Sultan Ahmed, Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record - For Respondent No. 1. 
Not represented - Respondent Nos. 2-12.
parties:
Israil and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Ali Asgar and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. This petition for leave to appeal is by the 2nd party to the proceeding initiated under section 145 CrPC. The proceeding under section 145 CrPC was initiated at the instance of the respondent in respect of the land described in the schedule attached to the petition of complaint which was filed alleging that the 2nd party (petitioners herein) threatened the bargader of the 1st party-respondent and thus there was apprehension of breach of peace. On receiving the application the Magistrate drew up a proceeding under section 144 CrPC and directed the officer-in-charge, Porsha PS to enquire and report and that further directed the parties to maintain status quo. On receipt of the report of the officer-in-charge of the Porsha PS the Magistrate drew up a proceeding under section 145 CrPC and thereupon made the order for attachment of the land and that appointed officer-in-charge, Porsha PS receiver in respect of the land attached. The Magistrate by the order dated 9th April, 1994 directed officer-in-charge, Porsha to make inquiry for determination which of the parties was in actual possession of the property. Parties to the proceeding filed written statements. Both the parties examined witnesses. Finally, the Magistrate by order dated 2nd September, 1998 directed the receiver to make over possession of the land to the 2nd party in the proceeding on the findings that prior to the appointment of the receiver the 2nd party was in possession. As against the order dated 2nd September, 1998 of the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Naogaon the 1st party respondent moved the Court of Sessions in revisional jurisdiction, in Criminal Revision No. 127 of 1998 and the same was finally heard by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. The learned Additional Sessions Judge set aside the order of the Magistrate on the findings that the Magistrate arrived at the findings as to possession of the land in the proceeding by the 2nd party without discussing the evidence of the 1st party and that relied on the report of the receiver and the report of the officer-in-charge of Porsha PS on the basis whereof proceeding under section 145 CrPC started. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on the finding that exception in no way be taken to reasoning upon which the learned Additional Sessions Judge set aside the order of the Magistrate making direction to the receiver to make over possession of the land to the 2nd party. As seen from the materials on record learned Magistrate did not arrive at a definite finding as to possession of the parties in the proceeding 2 months prior to the initiation of the proceeding. The High Court Division also rejected the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that in making the order for attachment of the land and that appointing receiver in respect of the land, the learned Additional Sessions Judge acted in excess of his jurisdiction arriving at the finding that a court of revision as per different provisions of the CrPC is competent to exercise power to alter or reverse or may amend the order of a court subordinate to it and make an order which is just and proper and in that view of the matter the learned Additional Sessions Judge had not acted in accordance with law in setting aside the order of the learned Magistrate and thereupon making the order of attachment of the land over which the parties were in dispute and that making order appointing receiver to manage the property.
